update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency scientific inventions, medical discoveries, and their originators for General Science Static GK.

physics_and_chemistry.key_fact: Discovered through cathode ray tube experiments.
Eugen Goldstein discovered positive rays earlier, but Rutherford identified and named the proton.
Completed the basic atomic model; won him the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1935.
Discovered accidentally while experimenting with vacuum tubes; won the first Nobel Prize in Physics.
Discovered spontaneous radioactivity in uranium salts.
Marie Curie remains the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields (Physics and Chemistry).
Arranged elements by atomic mass and left gaps for elements that had not yet been discovered.
Invented as a safer way to harness nitroglycerin; the profits funded the Nobel Prizes.

biology_and_medicine.key_fact: Discovered accidentally from a mold (Penicillium notatum) that killed Staphylococcus bacteria.
The world's first successful vaccine; developed using the cowpox virus.
Salk developed the dead-virus vaccine; Sabin later developed the live-attenuated oral drops (OPV).
Developed the germ theory of disease and the first vaccine for rabies.
Made safe blood transfusions possible; won the Nobel Prize in Physiology/Medicine.
First to describe accurately how blood is pumped around the body by the heart.
Discovered in Toronto; transformed Type 1 diabetes from a fatal disease to a manageable condition.
Based heavily on the X-ray crystallography data captured by Rosalind Franklin.
Invented because he was uncomfortable placing his ear directly on a female patient's chest.

technology_and_computing.key_fact: Designed the 'Analytical Engine', considered the first mechanical computer concept. (Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm for it).
Invented while working at CERN to help scientists share data globally.
First successful bi-directional transmission of clear speech.
Demonstrated the first working mechanical television system.
Did not invent the first lightbulb, but invented the first commercially practical and long-lasting incandescent bulb.
Achieved the first sustained, controlled, powered heavier-than-air manned flight at Kitty Hawk.
Developed the first practical wireless telegraphy system based on Hertz's discovery of radio waves.
Vastly improved Thomas Newcomen's design, sparking the Industrial Revolution.
